::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 5 1898  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Hampshire Record Office: Heathcote Family Scrapbooks: 63M84/234/65
:::

My dear [Ellie](people/person_663.qmd)
I am delighted to hear of the Medallion![^1]

Have you seen Sir Herbert Maxwell’s [book of the months](other_books/otherbook_738.qmd)-? He disbelieved the rod and someone ought to write to him. He watched [Mullins](people/person_2189.qmd) - and fancied he had discovered the places before. But [Lady Crawley](people/person_2188.qmd), the mother of [Mrs William Gibbs](people/person_557.qmd), who had the power only in that generation of the family laughed at it as imagination, and I believe Mrs Gibbs inherited it, but never spoke of it. [Mrs Monroe](people/person_1033.qmd) had Mullins to find water at Colden Common and he did. All the servants tried under his tuition but only one maid succeeded.

I am doing our Birds with anecdotes if possible to add to the book.

[Helen](people/person_1613.qmd) has a copy of [illegible] marked by her [father](people/person_1624.qmd) and can complete the set. There really is much to say of them.

Your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: A medallion is mentioned in *John Keble's Parishes*, 3, which is the book under discussion here.
